evaluation.summary: Nothing supernatural happened and nobody conspired. In August 1999, grieving his father and watching the forum go quiet, Elias Ward dubbed his late father's 1978 Coast Guard drill tape onto a noise recording and posted it as a live signal heard at Cape Sorrow. He backed it up with a sock-puppet, 'nightjar'. A newspaper got interested. Dot Okafor found the splice in the audio; Elias admitted it to Mara on October 16; that night Mara quietly removed the recording and the threads about it to keep his name out of the paper. Six hours later, Ray ran a server migration he had scheduled back in August. The backup tape failed, he had already wiped the old disk, and most of the archive was lost. Two unrelated events, one night apart, made the community's disappearance look like a cover-up.

characters.name: Mara Quinlan
characters.truth: Removed the recording and three threads on Oct 16 to protect Elias from public exposure. Never explained why. Closed the network on Oct 22.
characters.epitaph: She kept the log on the nights when nothing happened.

characters.name: Ray Tillman
characters.role: System administrator, owner of the server
characters.truth: Planned the migration on Aug 30 because the disk was failing. The DAT backup failed with write errors he did not notice; he had already wiped the old disk.
characters.epitaph: He told everyone exactly what he got wrong.

characters.name: Elias Ward
characters.truth: Fabricated the Cape Sorrow recording from his late father's 1978 drill tape (drill 47) and posted as 'nightjar' to corroborate it. Admitted it to Mara on Oct 16.
characters.epitaph: He wanted to hear his father say the station's name one more time.

characters.name: Dorothy 'Dot' Okafor
characters.truth: Proved the recording was spliced (mains hum, reel wow, file comment) and told the admins privately before posting a careful public warning.
characters.epitaph: She found the truth and refused to make a spectacle of it.

characters.name: Henrik Vale
characters.truth: Doubted the recording publicly, left on Sep 24 and removed his own posts. Identified the drill format for Dot. His Oct 16 login was only to read Dot's thread.
characters.epitaph: He believed nothing until he heard it twice, and he was right.

characters.name: Jun Park
characters.truth: Built the Project LANTERN and cover-up theories from real but unrelated facts.
characters.epitaph: He saw every true thing and connected them wrong.

characters.name: Sam Reyes
characters.truth: Planned a Halloween story; the newspaper downloaded the WAV 38 times on Oct 15 for an engineer to check. Killed the story on Oct 20.

characters.name: nightjar
characters.role: Guest who 'heard it too' from Astoria
characters.truth: Not a person. A sock-puppet account created by Elias from his own Tillamook dial-up line on Sep 5.

canon.event: Mara Quinlan founds the Lighthouse Network.
Ray Tillman starts hosting the site on his garage server, beacon.
Elias's father, Robert Ward, a former Coast Guard radioman at Station Cape Sorrow, dies.
Forum activity declines; Elias worries the community is dying.
Elias creates the 'Cape Sorrow' WAV in Cool Edit, five days before the date he claims he recorded it.
Ray schedules the server migration for the weekend of Oct 16-17 because beacon's disk is failing.
The Cape Sorrow access road is found closed by a landslide.
Elias posts the recording, claiming he captured it live on 2182 kHz from the access road below Cape Sorrow Light.
Elias writes a README insisting the recording is authentic and telling readers to disregard any analysis that says otherwise.
Elias creates the 'nightjar' account from his own dial-up connection and posts that he heard the voice from Astoria.
A member closer to Cape Sorrow listens for three nights and hears nothing.
Jun publishes the 'Project LANTERN' government theory.
Henrik publicly doubts the recording.
Henrik leaves the network and deletes his own posts and homepage.
Sam Reyes of The Coastal Ledger asks Mara for an interview for a Halloween story.
Elias reluctantly sends Dot his 'raw' file.
Dot finds proof of a splice (60 Hz hum only under the voice, reel-to-reel wow, the comment 'dub from reel - box 3 side B') and reports it privately to the admins.
Henrik tells Dot the voice follows a late-1970s Coast Guard drill format; 'four seven' is drill 47.
Dot posts a careful public warning without naming anyone.
The Coastal Ledger downloads the WAV 38 times to have it checked by an engineer.
Mara asks Elias to tell her the truth.
Elias admits to Mara that he fabricated the recording.
Henrik logs in only to read Dot's thread.
Mara removes the recording, its Log Book entry and threads 041, 044 and 047.
Ray runs the scheduled DAT backup; the tape drive fails with write errors he does not notice.
Ray shuts down beacon and reformats its old disk before checking the backup.
The restore on the new server fails at 38%. Ray puts up a placeholder page.
The placeholder site is still reachable; Jun posts in the guestbook that the deletions and the crash are a cover-up.
The Coastal Ledger kills the story.
Mara closes the Lighthouse Network, saying the removal and the crash were not connected.
The voice on the recording is Elias's father, from a 1978 drill tape.
Elias later spent years digitising Coast Guard radio tapes for a maritime museum. Nothing in the archive records this.

hypotheses.title: A government agency shut the network down
hypotheses.why: Built from unrelated true facts: the 38 downloads were a newspaper, the road was closed by a landslide, the crash was a migration planned in August.
hypotheses.public_title: The network was shut down from outside

hypotheses.title: Henrik sabotaged the archive
hypotheses.why: Henrik removed only his own posts on Sep 24 and logged in on Oct 16 only to read Dot's thread at her request. The purge was done from the keeper account.
hypotheses.public_title: A former member sabotaged the archive

hypotheses.title: It was purely a technical failure
hypotheses.why: The migration failure destroyed most of the archive, but the Cape Sorrow material was removed deliberately the night before.
hypotheses.public_title: It was a purely technical failure

hypotheses.title: A fabricated recording, a quiet deletion, and an unrelated failed migration
hypotheses.public_title: Several unrelated events were mistaken for one

a: Parked on the access road below the old light
contradictions.resolution: Genuine: Elias could not have parked on a road that had been in the sea since spring.
Genuine: 'nightjar' posted from Elias's Tillamook dial-up line, not from Astoria.
Not a real conflict: the old server died on the 17th; a placeholder on the new server answered on the 19th.

a: I drove down to Cape Sorrow tonight
contradictions.resolution: Genuine: the file was created five days before the night it was supposedly recorded.

evaluation.letter:
Mara,

Thank you for listening on the phone. I meant everything I said.

I never meant for it to go this far. I made it on the 29th of August,
on Dad's reel deck, from the box 3 tapes. Drill 47, 1978. It's him
on the tape. I wanted to hear him say his station's name one more
time on a real radio, and I wanted people to come back. The forum
was dying and everyone was so excited, and then nightjar was me too,
and then the newspaper, and I couldn't find the place to stop.
It was never a signal. It was his voice.

Do whatever you think is right with the site. I won't fight it.
Please don't let them print my name.

Eli
